html:
The Bolivian gas war was a wave of protests in 2003 against a plan to export Bolivia's natural gas through a port in Chile. It forced President Gonzalo Sánchez de Lozada to resign on 17 October 2003.

Huge gas reserves had been found in the southeast. Many Bolivians felt that foreign companies would take the profits, as with silver and tin before, and resented using a port in Chile, which had taken Bolivia's coast in the War of the Pacific. Aymara residents of El Alto blocked the roads into La Paz. Soldiers killed some 60 people.

The president fled to the United States. His successors held a referendum on gas, and in 2006 Evo Morales nationalised it. The gas war followed the water war in remaking the politics of Bolivia.
sum: The Bolivian gas war was a wave of protests in 2003 against a plan to export Bolivia's natural gas through a port in Chile. It forced President Gonzalo Sánchez de Lozada to resign on 17 October 2003.
